manuscript_claim_lines.ex_ante_claim: Reserve exposure orders the three coins ex ante: USDC held direct SVB exposure, DAI was pinned to USDC through the peg-stability module, and USDT held none. That gives the ex-ante fragility ordering USDC, DAI, USDT.
manuscript_claim_lines.realized_ordering_claim: Troughs are \$0.877, \$0.886, and \$0.992 in that order.

claim_type_determination: FULL RANK ORDER over a linked pair and one free coin. The ex-ante paragraph (fc27short.tex:506) states an explicit 3-way ranking (USDC most fragile, DAI next, USDT least) and the realized-ordering paragraph (fc27short:508) reports the realized troughs as consistent with that ex-ante exposure ranking. DAI is mechanically linked to USDC through the PSM (the DAI-contagion result), so it is not an exchangeable draw and the USDC-DAI pair moves as one block. The null space is the 2 placements of USDT relative to that block, not the 6 permutations of 3 free items.

permutations.description: USDT least fragile, outside the linked USDC-DAI block
USDT more fragile than the linked USDC-DAI block

note: 1/2 under the ruled null (D16). The free comparison is USDT against the linked USDC-DAI pair, because the DAI-contagion result establishes DAI's break runs through its USDC exposure rather than an independent run. Scoring the match against all 6 permutations would treat DAI as exchangeable, which the paper's own contagion argument denies.
